note: The Nimitz's deck layout, read by engine.ts and by the model tools (tools/nimitz/ship.py). Deck frame in metres after the model's lateral squash: x forward, z to starboard; headings in degrees, positive to port. A catapult's x, z is where the nose wheel rests on its shuttle; stroke is its throw in metres and speed its end speed in m/s; its deflector is the painted box the blast deflector lies in, width across the track and depth along it. elevators: where each deck-edge elevator's platform meets the deck edge (the outboard edge of the platform the model paints, 26.3-26.5 m long, as the real ones are 26 m) and its side (1 starboard, -1 port); the catwalk stops and the edge lights run along it. rafts: how many life-raft canisters hang on the catwalks, as many as the catwalks between the elevators and sponsons hold (the model builder's estimate of 242 needed catwalk alongside the elevator platforms); build_carrier.py racks them and edgecheck.py counts them. cabs: where each catapult control cab stands and which way it points; cabs.py has their size. build_carrier.py writes the outline, traced from the deck it builds; the rest is set by hand.

catapults.note: Starboard bow, from the 1:200 plan (2026-07-10): its track line starts just aft of this spot and runs to the bow water-brake slot. The model's own painted track sits 3.9 m to starboard on no plan feature. The deflector's starboard side comes in 1.75 m, clear of elevator 1's border: the model's elevator 1 sits about 10 m forward of the plan's.
Port bow, where the carrier start spawns: located in game (2026-07-07) and fitted to the track's own triangles.
Starboard waist: located in game (2026-07-07) and fitted to the track's own triangles.
Port waist: heading as read in game (2026-07-07), z from the plan's track line (2026-07-10).

landing.note: line: the landing centreline, its aft point then its forward point, on the model's painted stripe (a least-squares fit through its yellow centreline segments, 8.99 degrees; the real angled deck is 9.05). wires: where each cross-deck pendant crosses the line, square to it: the four-wire CVN-68 fit, 11.7 m apart, the first 51 m from the round-down. span: a pendant's length between its sheaves, centred on the line as the plan draws them, which stands the sheaves just outside the 22 m landing area.

ols.note: The lens on its port-side bracket, measured off the model's own lens. model: the ship model carries the bracket, so the engine draws only the lights.

cabs.note: Bow: between cats 1 and 2 at the plan's x, centred between the dashed lines that run between them, its heading halfway between theirs.

Waist: the deck-edge cab outboard of cat 4 (NAVAIR 00-80T-120's deckedge ICCS), its inboard side on the painted deck-edge line as the plan draws it, but 4.7 m aft of the plan's x: the traced deck edge notches in by 1.3 m at the plan's spot, and the cab's plate keeps 0.15 m inside it. A jet's main wheels on cat 4 pass about 2.4 m clear, as on the plan.

texture.note: The deck texture's extent: the baked deck's u runs from x[0] to x[1], v from z[0] to z[1].
